title: From Coverage to Causes: Data-Centric Fuzzing for JavaScript Engines

edges.target: Fuzzilli (Gross et al.)
edges.ref: [16] Samuel Gross, Simon Koch, Lukas Bernhard, Thorsten Holz, Martin Johns. Fuzzilli: Fuzzing for javascript jit compiler vulnerabilities. NDSS, 2023.
edges.evidence: Fuzzilli and DIE both found one crash in ~94 and ~87 hours, respectively. ... compared the execution rate of our approach with a coverage-guided baseline (Fuzzilli)

edges.target: FuzzJIT (Wang et al.)
edges.ref: [8] Junjie Wang, Zhiyi Zhang, Shuang Liu, Xiaoning Du, Junjie Chen. FuzzJIT: Oracle-Enhanced fuzzing for JavaScript engine JIT compiler. USENIX Security 23.
edges.evidence: In our experiments, FuzzJIT was not able to find any crashes within the 96 hour fuzzing campaign.

edges.target: DIE (Park et al.)
edges.ref: [6] Soyeon Park, Wen Xu, Insu Yun, Daehee Jang, Taesoo Kim. Fuzzing javascript engines with aspect-preserving mutation. IEEE S&P 2020, pages 1629-1642.
edges.evidence: Fuzzilli and DIE both found one crash in ~94 and ~87 hours, respectively.

edges.target: Fuzzilli (base fuzzer)
edges.ref: [16] Samuel Gross, Simon Koch, Lukas Bernhard, Thorsten Holz, Martin Johns. Fuzzilli: Fuzzing for javascript jit compiler vulnerabilities. NDSS, 2023.
edges.evidence: This fuzzer was built on top of Fuzzilli, which has been utilized in multiple works in JS engine fuzzing

edges.target: XGBoost (Chen & Guestrin)
edges.ref: [50] Tianqi Chen and Carlos Guestrin. Xgboost: A scalable tree boosting system. KDD 2016, pages 785-794.
edges.evidence: We implemented M using the XGBoost Machine Learning model. ... We use the XGBoost feature importance score to answer RQ4.

edges.target: Scikit-learn (XGBoost sklearn estimator)
edges.ref: footnote 10: https://xgboost.readthedocs.io/en/stable/python/sklearn_estimator.html
edges.evidence: We implemented XGBoost using Scikit-learn. ... Scikit-learn's XGBoost includes the scale_pos_weight hyperparameter

edges.target: GPT-4.1 (OpenAI)
edges.ref: footnote 9: https://openai.com/index/gpt-4-1
edges.evidence: In Phase 2 and 3, we use GPT 4.1, the latest model available at the time of this study, to extract features.

edges.target: SHAP (Lundberg & Lee)
edges.ref: [47] Scott M Lundberg and Su-In Lee. A unified approach to interpreting model predictions. NeurIPS 30, 2017.
edges.evidence: we used SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to provide instance-specific guidance [47, 48]. For each parent seed, we identified the feature subset that SHAP deemed most responsible

edges.target: ShapFuzz (Zhang et al.)
edges.ref: [48] Kunpeng Zhang, Xiaogang Zhu, Xi Xiao, Minhui Xue, Chao Zhang, Sheng Wen. Shapfuzz: Efficient fuzzing via shapley-guided byte selection. arXiv:2308.09239, 2023.
edges.evidence: we used SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to provide instance-specific guidance [47, 48].

edges.target: jsvu (JavaScript engine Version Updater)
edges.ref: footnote 8: https://github.com/GoogleChromeLabs/jsvu
edges.evidence: Since building many versions of V8 takes substantial time, we prebuilt binaries provided by the JavaScript (engine) Version Updater (jsvu) tool.

edges.target: V8 JavaScript engine (with trace flags)
edges.ref: https://v8.dev (system under test; trace flags such as --trace-gc, --log-maps, --trace-ic)
edges.evidence: executes the input with the selected V8 tracing flags, captures the resulting log output, and parses it to construct the dynamic feature vector

edges.target: Chromium bug repository V8 vulnerability PoCs
edges.ref: footnotes 6-7: https://issues.chromium.org/issues?q=componentid:(1456800|...) status:(fixed|verified) type:vulnerability created:2019-01-01..2025-06-30
edges.evidence: We queried the Chromium bug repository with a search query which retrieves fixed or verified bug reports related to the vulnerabilities within the V8 runtime ... we obtained 220 reports.

edges.target: V8 mjsunit test suite (negative samples)
edges.ref: official V8 test suites, mjsunit (no formal reference; V8 source tree)
edges.evidence: the negative samples were collected from the official V8 test suites. Specifically, for each time-based fold ... the test cases from the mjsunit suite

edges.target: Walk-forward / time-ordered validation (Falessi et al.)
edges.ref: [49] Davide Falessi, Jacky Huang, Likhita Narayana, Jennifer Fong Thai, Burak Turhan. On the need of preserving order of data when validating within-project defect classifiers. EMSE 25(6), 2020.
edges.evidence: the data is divided into four folds for cross-validation with a walk-forward protocol [49].

edges.target: Aspect-preserving mutation (DIE, Park et al.)
edges.ref: [6] Soyeon Park, Wen Xu, Insu Yun, Daehee Jang, Taesoo Kim. Fuzzing javascript engines with aspect-preserving mutation. IEEE S&P 2020, pages 1629-1642.
edges.evidence: we extended the concept of aspect-preserving mutation proposed by Park et al. [6] to feature-preserving mutation.

edges.target: LLM-driven feature generation for tabular data (Nam et al.; Zhang et al.; LLM-FE)
edges.ref: [41] Nam et al. Optimized feature generation for tabular data via llms with decision tree reasoning. NeurIPS 37, 2024; [42] arXiv:2406.03505; [43] arXiv:2503.14434
edges.evidence: Inspired by the effectiveness of LLMs in feature discovery shown in recent studies [41-43], we propose an LLM-driven feature discovery approach using historical vulnerabilities.

edges.target: Wilcoxon rank-sum / Mann-Whitney test
edges.ref: [52] Frank Wilcoxon. Individual comparisons by ranking methods. Biometrics Bulletin 1(6), 1945; [53] Mann & Whitney, Ann. Math. Statist. 18, 1947.
edges.evidence: We statistically compared our methods using the Wilcoxon Rank-Sum test [52, 53].

edges.target: OptFuzz observation: no crashes on latest V8 (Wang et al.)
edges.ref: [5] Jiming Wang et al. OptFuzz: Optimization path guided fuzzing for JavaScript JIT compilers. USENIX Security 24, pages 865-882.
edges.evidence: Similar to Wang et al. [5], we observed that running the state-of-the-art fuzzers for a week on the latest V8 did not yield any crashes.

edges.target: Declining bug-discovery rates in mature software (Elahi & Wang)
edges.ref: [20] Haroon Elahi and Guojun Wang. Forward-porting and its limitations in fuzzer evaluation. Information Sciences 662:120142, 2024.
edges.evidence: an outcome that is consistent with recent studies showing declining rates of bug discovery in mature, heavily-tested software [5, 20]

edges.target: XGBoost vs deep learning on tabular data (Shwartz-Ziv & Armon)
edges.ref: [51] Ravid Shwartz-Ziv and Amitai Armon. Tabular data: Deep learning is not all you need. Information Fusion 81:84-90, 2022.
edges.evidence: Shwartz-Ziv and Armon showed that XGBoost can be as effective as deep learners for tabular data, in terms of both predictive performance and training time [51].

edges.target: Role identification improves LLM performance (GRACE, Lu et al.)
edges.ref: [44] Guilong Lu, Xiaolin Ju, Xiang Chen, Wenlong Pei, Zhilong Cai. Grace: Empowering llm-based software vulnerability detection with graph structure and in-context learning. JSS 212, 2024.
edges.evidence: Identification specifies the role of the LLM ... Lu et al., showed that identification significantly improves LLM's performance [44].

edges.target: LLMs fail to follow structural constraints (CRANE; Break-the-chain)
edges.ref: [45] Banerjee et al. Crane: Reasoning with constrained llm generation. arXiv:2502.09061, 2025; [46] Roh et al. Break-the-chain. arXiv:2506.06971, 2025.
edges.evidence: The reason we initially did not extract five flags is that LLMs often fail to follow structural constraints [45, 46]. Hence, we slightly relaxed the constraint and then curated the list.

edges.target: mjsunit as seed corpus / static seed features (Wen et al.)
edges.ref: [19] Ming Wen, Yongcong Wang, Yifan Xia, Hai Jin. Evaluating seed selection for fuzzing javascript engines. EMSE 28(6):133, 2023.
edges.evidence: The mjsunit test suit is widely used as seed corpus because it contains both simple and adversarial code [12, 19]. ... prioritizing valid input seeds with code structure ... is highly effective [19]

edges.target: Montage: buggy fragments come from regression tests (Lee et al.)
edges.ref: [12] Suyoung Lee, HyungSeok Han, Sang Kil Cha, Sooel Son. Montage: A neural network language Model-Guided JavaScript engine fuzzer. USENIX Security 20.
edges.evidence: Montage shows that most buggy fragments come from the JS engine tests ... Hence, using this makes our findings more meaningful compared to using trivial and easy-to-predict negative sample.

edges.target: Iterative validation improves LLM generalizability (Xu et al.; Step-Opt)
edges.ref: [57] Xu et al. Enhancing tool retrieval with iterative feedback from LLMs. arXiv:2406.17465, 2024; [58] Wu et al. Step-opt. arXiv:2506.17637, 2025.
edges.evidence: We mitigate this risk by iterative validation on unseen PoCs and manual curation, a strategy shown to improve LLM generalizability in other contexts [57, 58].

edges.target: Fuzzilli bug-finding cost: 17 bugs, six months, 500 CPU cores (Gross et al.)
edges.ref: [16] Samuel Gross, Simon Koch, Lukas Bernhard, Thorsten Holz, Martin Johns. Fuzzilli: Fuzzing for javascript jit compiler vulnerabilities. NDSS, 2023.
edges.evidence: Fuzzilli found over 17 bugs over the period of six months with 500 CPU cores [16]. ... When a fuzzer's search strategy is inefficient ... it must compensate with brute force computation.
edges.section: 3.2 Heuristic-Based Semantic Guidance Need Manual Effort

edges.target: DIE bug-finding cost: 48 bugs, 388-839 CPU cores, one week (Park et al.)
edges.ref: [6] Soyeon Park, Wen Xu, Insu Yun, Daehee Jang, Taesoo Kim. Fuzzing javascript engines with aspect-preserving mutation. IEEE S&P 2020, pages 1629-1642.
edges.evidence: DIE found 48 new bugs across major JS engines, but required 388-839 CPU cores and distributed processing over a week [6].
edges.section: 3.2 Heuristic-Based Semantic Guidance Need Manual Effort

edges.target: Coverage-guidance assumption: new paths correlate with new vulnerabilities (FairFuzz, Lemieux & Sen; Fuzzilli/DIE/OptFuzz)
edges.ref: [3] Caroline Lemieux and Koushik Sen. Fairfuzz: A targeted mutation strategy for increasing greybox fuzz testing coverage. ASE 2018, pages 475-485. (also [5, 6, 16])
edges.evidence: its success depends on the assumption that new paths correlate with new vulnerabilities [3]. ... Over 10 runs, only ~22% vulnerable and 1400 benign seeds were selected on average.

edges.target: DIE's aspect preservation does not generalize (PatchFuzz, Wang et al.)
edges.ref: [7] Junjie Wang, Yuhan Ma, Xiaofei Xie, Xiaoning Du, Xiangwei Zhang. Patchfuzz: Patch fuzzing for javascript engines. arXiv:2505.00289, 2025.
edges.evidence: DIE [6] focuses on preserving 'aspects' ... This was later shown not to generalize to other classes of vulnerabilities [7], suggesting the existence of additional 'aspects'.

edges.target: Coverage instrumentation is a primary source of fuzzer slowdown (RIFF, Wang et al.)
edges.ref: [56] Mingzhe Wang, Jie Liang, Chijin Zhou, Yu Jiang, Rui Wang, Chengnian Sun, Jiaguang Sun. RIFF: Reduced instruction footprint for coverage-guided fuzzing. USENIX ATC 2021, pages 147-159.
edges.evidence: This is because the coverage-instrumented engine, which is a primary source of significant slowdown [56], can mostly be avoided in feature-guided executions.

notes: Ganguly & Menzies (no self-reuse); all 8 v1 sanitychecks became numericfact except the OptFuzz no-crash observation, which the paper regenerated itself (replication); new refutation-polarity edges capture the paper's case against coverage guidance and the Fuzzilli/DIE brute-force cost numbers; no theory edges exist.
